articles.title: Essential Energy gets green light to trial 300 streetlights with built-in EV chargers
articles.summary: Essential Energy, the regional New South Wales power network, has approval to trial 300 streetlights with the charger built into the pole, aimed at towns where many drivers have nowhere off the street to plug in. The trial is paid for by the network and the Australian Renewable Energy Agency rather than household power bills, but it does not start until 2028, and the chargers have to be sold to a private operator or removed when the waiver ends.

articles.title: Brisbane apartment owners can now install EV chargers after Origin retrofit
articles.summary: Owners at the Urban Edge apartments in Kelvin Grove, Brisbane, can now add a charger in their own parking bay after Origin installed shared cabling and load management, with ARENA covering half of the $700,000 retrofit. The body corporate already approved the work, and each owner pays about $5,000 for their bay, which is the kind of building-wide upgrade apartment and condo residents usually cannot do on their own.

articles.title: In-kerb EV charge points to be trialled in East Lothian
articles.summary: Three chargers built flush into the kerb are now live in East Lothian, Scotland, including one on a residential street, in a trial aimed at the nearly one in three UK households with no driveway. Drivers start a session with the same apps as the council's other chargers, and the partners are measuring whether a flat kerb unit can serve street-parked cars without cluttering the sidewalk.

articles.title: Home charger sharing can help bridge the UK's EV divide
articles.summary: Zemo Partnership is urging people with a home charger to share it with neighbours who have no driveway, so those drivers can plug in nearby, often for less than a public charger, while the host earns from a plug that otherwise sits idle. Hosts set the price and accept each booking, and groups including the AA and EVA England say the unused private chargers could help the millions of UK households that cannot install their own.

articles.title: Chevy, GMC, and Cadillac EV owners can now plug and charge at Electrify America
articles.summary: Chevy, GMC, and Cadillac drivers enrolled in GM Energy Pass can now start a session at Electrify America by plugging in, with power flowing in about 45 seconds and no separate app at the stall. It is live on GM cars with a CCS port, and GM says NACS-port cars get the same Electrify America feature in early 2027, which matters for apartment and street-parked drivers who do most of their charging in public.

articles.title: Ku-ring-gai Council installs 21 kerbside EV charging ports
articles.summary: Ku-ring-gai Council has switched on 21 new kerbside charging ports across Sydney's north, paid for by a NSW government grant and aimed at residents who have no garage or driveway. Drivers need to bring their own Type 2 cable, and the mayor said the point is to put chargers on the street where people already park so an EV is practical without off-street parking.
